prerequisites: Prior knowledge in mathematics, statistics, and probability is recommended.

learning_outcomes.text: Understanding and interpreting texts and data, developing skills for their concretization and clear and succinct presentation.
Ability to transmit concepts, ideas, processes, etc., related to Industrial Engineering orally and in writing, clearly and correctly.
Ability for teamwork and capacity for the development of multidisciplinary projects.
Ability to incorporate new knowledge in the area of Industrial Engineering, based on the acquired training and necessary for the evolution of technique.

syllabus_topics: Calculation and expression of measurement process uncertainty
Estimation of measurement uncertainty by computerized methods
Use of advanced tolerances and their application to functional parts
Technical fundamentals and functionalities of the main types of measurement equipment in advanced manufacturing
Measurement and inspection methods including non-contact, 3D scanning and/or image-based
Management and organization of metrology laboratories
Integration of metrology in the context of quality
teaching_methods: Lectures (exposition, explanation, and exemplification of content)
Resolution of exercises and practical cases with student participation and specialized software use
Personal study of theory and problems/practices
Preparation of problem sets or practical cases proposed by the professor, including those requiring software use
Preparation of oral presentations for seminars
Search and consultation of bibliographic and/or technical standards information
Debate and student participation in class

assessment_methods.method: Continuous assessment activities (e.g., practical cases, seminars, laboratory/simulation practices, software practices, research assignments, external visits)
Objective evaluation tests (written tests or tests via the virtual campus)

assessment_rules: A minimum grade may be required in each evaluation element (minimum criterion), which will never exceed 5 points out of 10 and will be announced to students in advance.
